angularDiameterSource: Limb-darkened angular diameter 6.039 ± 0.019 mas measured on Sirius A with VLTI/VINCI by Kervella et al. (2003), A&A 408, 681; at 2.6371 pc this is the record's radius.
distanceSource: Inverse of the Hipparcos new-reduction parallax 379.21 +/- 1.58 mas (van Leeuwen 2007, A&A 474, 653; 2007A&A...474..653V) via SIMBAD
radiusSource: Radius: the limb-darkened angular diameter 6.039 +/- 0.019 mas that Kervella et al. (2003, A&A 408, 681) measure on Sirius A with VLTI/VINCI, at the Hipparcos new-reduction parallax 379.21 +/- 1.58 mas (2.6371 pc): 1,191,189 km, 1.712 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius (the paper gives 1.711 +/- 0.013). No gravitational parameter is adopted. presentationUp: no rotation axis is measured, so the presentation frame puts the display axis (celestial north at the star) up.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Effective temperature 9845 ± 64 K from Davis et al. 2011 (PASA 28, 58; https://doi.org/10.1071/AS10010), abstract: the SUSI and VLTI limb-darkened diameter 6.041 ± 0.017 mas with the bolometric flux. The radius source, Kervella et al. 2003, adopts a temperature rather than measuring one.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray; no picture of the photosphere is cast.
